claims: The Space Shuttle Challenger disaster occurred on January 28, 1986.
The Challenger orbiter disintegrated 73 seconds after liftoff.
The disintegration killed all seven crew members.
A failed O-ring seal in the right solid rocket booster caused the fatal structural failure.
Cold temperatures compromised the O-ring seal.
The Challenger disaster forced a 32-month shutdown of the shuttle program.
The Challenger shuttle broke up at 11:38 a.m. EST.
The Challenger shuttle broke up 46,000 feet above the Atlantic Ocean.
A cold-induced failure of the O-ring seal allowed hot gas to breach the solid rocket booster.
The hot gas breach led to the rupture of the external fuel tank.
The seven Challenger crew members were Dick Scobee, Michael J. Smith, Ronald McNair, Ellison Onizuka, Judy Resnik, Greg Jarvis, and Christa McAuliffe.
The last known words from the Challenger crew came from pilot Michael J. Smith, who said "Uh oh."
A comment from Commander Dick Scobee followed, which was cut off.
The Challenger crew cabin was found in the ocean.
It is believed the Challenger astronauts died from the massive impact (over 200 mph) of the cabin with the ocean, rather than the initial explosion.
The Challenger tragedy caused the US government to suspend the space shuttle program for over two years.
The Rogers Commission identified the technical cause as the O-ring failure.
The Rogers Commission highlighted that NASA management ignored engineer warnings regarding the cold weather.
Christa McAuliffe was the "teacher in space."
Christa McAuliffe's lessons were performed in space in 2018.
A large segment of the Challenger was discovered on the ocean floor in 2022.
There is an upcoming limited series about the Challenger mission starring Kristen Stewart as Sally Ride.
The limited series is in development.
